newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP may delay corporate tax cut - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP may delay corporate tax cut - report.

text.p: A senior policymaker of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party indicated on Wednesday that corporate tax cuts promised by the party during the election campaign in October may not be carried out until 1998/99 or later, a Japanese news agency said.

"We promised the tax cut during the general elections and we were thinking of carrying it out from 1997/98. Now, we are being pressured into giving excuses that we will implement it sometime before the next elections," Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the LDP's Policy Research Council, was quoted as saying by Jiji news agency.

Yamasaki also said that the government will have to scrap special income tax cuts currently worth two trillion yen annually, in light of the government's plan to reduce its fiscal debt, Jiji reported.

He added that a supplementary budget with some five trillion yen worth of public works should be compiled in the current fiscal year ending in March, to assist smaller companies and the rebuilding of areas devastated by last year's earthquake in western Japan, Jiji said.
